note: Primitive camping area in the middle of the area off the gravel area road: six gravel pull-in spurs in a mown opening with a privy alongside, and open woods around. No tables or water. The bottoms along Saline Creek and the Osage flood in spring. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: one designated camping area (map symbol, GIS point) with a privy and six built gravel pull-in spurs on imagery - not a lot. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit; privy written; phone matches. Small pin move to the spurs flagged.
flags: INCLUSION (stays): page 'Camping: Individual Campsites'; brochure: 'Camping is allowed anytime in designated camping areas shown on map. These may or may not have defined campsites. No amenities are provided.' The map (11/18/2021) draws one Primitive Camping symbol at the central lot cluster with Privy and Disabled Accessible symbols. GIS layer 27: one point at 38.28312,-92.44367 = stored pin. On the leaf-off frame, 110-170 m north-west of the pin, a gravel spur road has six herringbone pull-in spurs (three each side, each about 12-15 m long) in a mown opening, a small building on its own gravel pad (the privy, GIS lot at 38.28386,-92.44454) and a tent pitched beside the spurs. Spur length is an imagery estimate; nothing is published.

PIN MOVE (small): stored 38.28312,-92.44367 (the GIS point) is in open woods about 30 m off the road with no pad. The pull-in spurs are at about 38.28396,-92.44521, roughly 160 m west-north-west. Proposed new pin 38.28396,-92.44521.
WATERFRONT: not waterfront stands - upland opening, no water near.
SEASON: stored year_round (manual) stands; 'camping is allowed anytime'.
